sources.text:
October 3, 2026 - Korean Peninsula
Source article image alternative text: Korean Peninsula
Tweet
Share
Suspended sediment floated off the western coast of the Korean Peninsula on October 2, 2026, when the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) on NASA’s Aqua satellite acquired this true-color image of the region. Sediment, which looks muddy tan when it floats near the surface and green as it sinks, appears thickest in the Yellow Sea, especially off the coast of South Korea.
The mountains of the Korean Peninsula lies in the east, giving rise to most of the major rivers of the region. These rivers course westward, gathering sediment, which ultimately spills into the yellow sea. South Korea’s Han River, the fourth longest river on the peninsula. The mouth of the Han forms broad tidal flats where it meets the sea near the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), which forms the border between North and South Korea.

COMMERCIAL USE
For use of NASA images clearances may be necessary for images that include any NASA logos or NASA employees to be used as cover art or in promotional content. Otherwise, NASA imagery can be generally used editorially within published works that are not promotional in nature.
If the NASA material is to be used for commercial purposes, including advertisements, it must not explicitly or implicitly convey NASA’s endorsement of commercial goods or services.
Commercials and promotional content cannot be filmed on NASA property.
For commercial use of NASA’s images, intellectual property, emblems, or logos on merchandise or products refer to the Merchandise Guidelines and Approvals page.
Media including Identifiable Persons
If a NASA image, audio, video or media includes an identifiable person, using the media for commercial purposes may infringe that person’s right of privacy or publicity, and permission should be obtained from the person.
Astronauts or employees who are currently employed by NASA cannot have their names, likenesses or other personality traits displayed or position title used on any commercial products, advertisements, promotional material or commercial product packaging.
For guidance on commercial use on merchandise please refer to NASA’s Merchandise Guidelines.
For more information on using NASA content for commercial purposes, please read NASA Advertising Guidelines and Merchandise Guidelines. Any questions regarding use of NASA content, or any NASA emblems, should be directed to nasa-merchandise-&-brand-team@mail.nasa.gov in NASA’s Office of Communications at NASA Headquarters in Washington.
Astronauts or NASA employees who are retired from the agency can grant permission for the use of their names, likenesses or other personality traits in their discretion, but their former affiliation with NASA may not be used to promote any product, service or activity. For deceased astronauts or employees, their estates may retain rights in the deceased person’s name, likeness or other personality traits, so permission may still be needed.
There are many images (moving and still) which have been made publicly available by NASA featuring astronauts in space suits where the astronauts face may be shielded or not easily recognizable, but where some other aspect of the photo may indicate the astronaut’s identity – like a name tag or simply the historical context of the photo. In such a case, the restrictions set forth above may still be applicable, so permission may still be necessary.

Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) and Cryptocurrency
As a U.S. government agency, NASA makes its imagery and video publicly available for educational and information purposes, however, since NFTs are, in essence, digital tokens owned by someone as a “one of a kind” digital asset, NASA doesn’t wish for its materials to be used for these purposes. The agency also doesn’t approve any merchandising applications involving NFTs, and it’s unlawful to falsely claim copyright or other rights in NASA materials.
NASA will not promote or endorse or appear to promote or endorse a commercial product, service or activity. This includes cryptocurrency.
Further, astronauts or employees who are currently employed by NASA cannot have their names, likenesses or other personality traits displayed or position title used on any commercial products, advertisements, promotional material or commercial product packaging.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Applications
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Applications
NASA is committed to transparency, open science, and making data available to everyone. While a wealth of public information is available for use in artificial intelligence (AI) applications, it’s important to understand the following when using our data for AI development:
Attribution: NASA cannot verify the accuracy of information once it’s incorporated into a large language model. Therefore, attribution of the information directly to NASA is not permitted. Similarly, NASA does not permit our Insignia (i.e., NASA Meatball, Worm logotype, or Seal) to appear with AI generated imagery or in the training of AI tools. To promote transparency, NASA strongly encourages AI-generated products maintain a marking indicating the product is AI generated.
Source Disclosure (No Permission Implied): As a statement of fact, you can acknowledge your AI tool includes NASA source material, but do not imply any review or permission was granted by NASA for its specific use.
Accuracy Disclaimer: It’s important to clarify that NASA is not responsible for the accuracy of the information generated by your AI model.
AI Model Attribution: All outputs from the AI model should be attributed to the AI product itself, not NASA. References like “according to NASA” or similar are prohibited in AI products.
Endorsement: Use of NASA content to train AI models does not constitute endorsement by NASA.
By following these guidelines, you can ensure transparency and responsible use of our public information in your AI applications.
IMAGE ACCESS
NASA has extensive image and video galleries online, including historic images, current missions, astronomy pictures, Earth images and ways to search for NASA images. Generally, each mission and program has a video and image collection on the topic page. For example, Space Station videos can be found at https://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/station/videos/index.html. Content can also be found on our extensive social media channels.

paragraphs.text: Kuvan tallensi Aqua-satelliitin MODIS-mittalaite 2. lokakuuta 2026. NASAn kuvaesittelyn mukaan lähellä pintaa oleva sedimentti näkyy luonnollisia värejä esittävässä kuvassa ruskehtavana ja syvemmälle painuva sedimentti vihreänä.

NASA selittää sedimentin kulkeutumista niemimaan jokien avulla: monet suuret joet saavat alkunsa idän vuoristoalueilta ja virtaavat länteen. Ne keräävät matkallaan maa-ainesta ja kuljettavat sitä Keltaiseenmereen.
Yksi näistä joista on Etelä-Korean Han. Kuvaesittelyn mukaan sen suulla on laajoja vuorovesitasankoja lähellä Pohjois- ja Etelä-Korean välistä demilitarisoitua vyöhykettä.

draft.summary: NASAn 3. lokakuuta julkaisema satelliittikuva näyttää merivedessä leijuvaa sedimenttiä Korean niemimaan länsipuolella. Edellisenä päivänä otetussa kuvassa sitä näkyy kuvaesittelyn mukaan eniten Etelä-Korean edustalla Keltaisellamerellä.
draft.title: Korean niemimaan sedimentti erottuu NASAn kuvassa

reasons: Otsikko on 49 merkkiä eli alle 60 merkin tavoitteen. Sedimenttihavainto ja Korean niemimaa ovat alussa, ja lähde A tukee otsikon sisältöä.

Lähde A tukee ingressin havaintopaikkaa, sedimentin runsautta erityisesti Etelä-Korean edustalla sekä kuvauspäivää 2.10.2026 ja julkaisuajankohtaa 3.10.2026. Aineisto on arviointipäivään nähden ajankohtainen.

Kaikkien kolmen kappaleen source_ids-merkintä A on asianmukainen: lähde nimeää Aqua-satelliitin ja MODIS-mittalaitteen, selittää sedimentin ruskehtavan ja vihreän värin, kuvaa jokien länteen suuntautuvan sedimentinkuljetuksen sekä mainitsee Han-joen suun vuorovesitasangot demilitarisoidun vyöhykkeen lähellä. Selitykset esitetään NASAn kuvaesittelyn tietoina, ei riippumattomasti vahvistettuina tutkimustuloksina.

Teksti on itsenäisesti suomeksi muotoiltu, neutraali ja ymmärrettävä. Tiede-luokitus sopii satelliittihavaintoa ja sedimentin kulkeutumista käsittelevään juttuun. Maantieteellistä soveltamisalaa ei laajenneta lähteen ulkopuolelle.

Luonnoksen koko kuvatietue vastaa lähdepaketin tietuetta. Kuvan päivämäärä ja tekijämaininta vastaavat lähdettä A, ja RIGHTS-asiakirjan toimituksellista käyttöä koskeva lupa tukee tämän NASA-kuvan käyttöä lähdemaininnalla. Kolme järjestettyä kuvakonseptia ja niiden hakumerkinnät on dokumentoitu. Valitun aidon kuvan täsmälliseen kuvatunnisteeseen sidottu pikseliarvio on 10/10 ja kuvaa juuri jutun länsirannikkoa ja sedimenttijuovia; yhteys ei perustu pelkkään paikkayhteyteen. Kolmannen konseptin vuorovesiuomien puuttuminen ei heikennä ensimmäiseen konseptiin perustuvan kuvan sopivuutta koko artikkeliin.
